BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). ## Executive view

The Seller’s package departs materially from the Buyer playbook and should not be accepted as a package. The most significant issues are:

1. materially weaker warranty thresholds, cap and limitation period;
2. improper application of the general limitations to title, fraud, indemnities, payment obligations, covenants, Tax and IP;
3. ineffective treatment of the Bluefen consent and Riverlark repayment/security releases;
4. omission of the employee bonuses and associated on-costs from funds flow;
5. overbroad deemed disclosure and Buyer-knowledge exclusions;
6. inadequate protection concerning Ironquay IP; and
7. reliance on an internal share register as proof of title.

The Disclosure Letter contains useful factual admissions, but it does not cure these issues. Several matters remain unverified or preliminary, and the underlying information is dated as at 22 September 2026. It should be refreshed before signing and again at Completion where appropriate.

## Detailed departures and recommended pushback

### 1. General warranty cap

**Seller position:** 20% of the purchase price, or AUD 4.8 million.

**Departure:** Our authorised opening position is 25%, or AUD 6 million. Although 20% is identified internally as a possible fallback, it can be used only with Amelia Frost’s prior written approval identifying the relevant draft. No such authority has been given.

**Pushback:** Reinstate a 25% general Warranty Claim cap. Do not treat the numerical match with the internal fallback as approval.

The cap must apply only to general Warranty Claims, not automatically to title, Tax, specific indemnities, payment obligations, Completion adjustments or covenant claims.

---

### 2. De minimis and basket

**Seller position:**

- AUD 25,000 de minimis;
- AUD 250,000 basket; and
- only the amount above the basket is recoverable.

**Departure:** The playbook requires:

- AUD 5,000 de minimis;
- AUD 50,000 aggregate basket; and
- a tipping basket, so the Seller is liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.

The Seller proposal is materially more restrictive on all three points.

**Pushback:** Amend to AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / first-dollar recovery once the basket is exceeded. Ensure related claims or claims arising from substantially the same facts are aggregated for de minimis purposes, so a single matter cannot be fragmented.

Title/fundamental claims and other agreed exceptional categories must sit outside both thresholds.

---

### 3. General warranty claims period

**Seller position:** 18 months after Completion.

**Departure:** The authorised position is 24 months. An 18-month period requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval, which has not been given.

**Pushback:** Reinstate 24 months. Include a conventional preservation rule: a sufficiently particularised claim notified before expiry survives until resolved, without an unreasonably short mandatory proceedings period.

---

### 4. Fundamental and title claims

**Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties would be subject to the general warranty cap and 18-month limitation period.

**Departure:** This directly conflicts with the playbook. Fundamental/title claims require:

- a separate 100% purchase-price cap;
- at least six years to bring claims; and
- exclusion from the general de minimis, basket and Buyer-knowledge limitations.

**Pushback:** Create an express separate regime for title, ownership, capacity and authority warranties. It should cover, at minimum:

- Seller ownership of all sale shares;
- valid issue and full payment of those shares;
- absence of Encumbrances and third-party interests;
- power, authority and binding obligations;
- ability to transfer full legal and beneficial title at Completion; and
- absence of options, conversion rights or other rights to acquire securities.

These claims should have a 100% cap, at least a six-year claim period, and no general thresholds or knowledge bar.

---

### 5. Fraud and deliberate misconduct

**Seller position:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

**Departure:** This could protect the Seller against fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct. That is prohibited by the playbook.

**Pushback:** Add an overriding carve-out, applying to the maximum extent enforceable, for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct. It must override:

- all liability caps;
- de minimis and baskets;
- time limits;
- exclusive-remedy provisions;
- non-reliance wording;
- Buyer-knowledge exclusions; and
- disclosure protections.

This is not a waivable negotiating point.

---

### 6. “All Claims” limitation architecture

**Seller position:** General limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded, with exclusive remedy and non-reliance also applying to all Claims.

**Departure:** This creates a hidden general-regime override and could unintentionally limit:

- title and fundamental claims;
- Tax claims;
- IP claims and the Ironquay indemnity;
- specific indemnities;
- Completion payment and adjustment obligations;
- repayment or reimbursement obligations;
- claims for breach of pre- or post-Completion covenants;
- debt-like or funds-flow obligations; and
- equitable or statutory rights that cannot properly be excluded.

Tax and IP remain open; they have not been settled merely because the Seller says so.

**Pushback:** Replace the blanket language with a clear liability matrix. Each cap, threshold and time limit should identify the claim category to which it applies. Preserve distinct regimes for:

1. general Warranty Claims;
2. title/fundamental claims;
3. Tax Claims;
4. IP claims and specific IP indemnities;
5. specific indemnities;
6. payment and price-adjustment obligations; and
7. covenant claims.

No unlimited Tax or IP liability should be conceded merely by rejecting the Seller’s general regime; those terms remain to be negotiated.

---

### 7. Disclosure standard

**Seller position:** Everything contained or referred to in the data room, statutory registers and public records is generally disclosed.

**Departure:** The playbook requires specific fair disclosure and rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.

A blanket disclosure makes the Buyer responsible for identifying the legal significance of documents spread across the data room. Public availability likewise does not establish that a matter was fairly disclosed against a particular warranty.

**Pushback:**

- Delete paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2 as general warranty disclosures.
- Require each exception to identify the relevant warranty and fairly disclose the nature and scope of the matter, including enough detail to understand its likely consequences.
- Data-room documents may support a specific disclosure only if clearly identified and cross-referenced.
- Reject disclosure by material merely “referred to” elsewhere.
- Reject public-register deemed disclosure and any prudent-search concept.
- Require a final indexed data-room copy and prohibit later alteration.
- Any supplemental disclosure should require Buyer review and should not automatically qualify warranties or remove termination rights.

The Seller’s reservation that disclosure does not admit breach or liability can remain only if it does not diminish the contractual fair-disclosure standard or the operative protections agreed for the relevant matter.

---

### 8. Buyer knowledge

**Seller position:** No claim for anything known by the Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records.

**Departure:** This is an impermissible constructive-knowledge and adviser-knowledge exclusion. It also duplicates the Seller’s overbroad disclosure regime.

**Pushback:** Delete the blanket knowledge exclusion. If any knowledge qualifier is retained:

- it should apply only to the actual knowledge of specifically named individuals;
- constructive knowledge, adviser knowledge and “discoverable” matters should be excluded;
- the Seller’s own warranty knowledge qualifiers should use named Seller knowledge persons who have made reasonable enquiries; and
- no knowledge bar should apply to title, capacity, authority, fraud, deliberate concealment or specific indemnities.

Buyer diligence should not relieve the Seller of responsibility for contractual warranties.

---

### 9. Bluefen consent

**Facts disclosed:** Bluefen represents approximately AUD 3.6 million of FY26 revenue, roughly 30%. The final written consent and evidence of satisfaction of its conditions are absent.

**Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent.

**Departure:** Given Bluefen’s materiality, reasonable endeavours and mere delivery are inadequate. A document called a consent may be conditional, revocable or ineffective unless clause 11.3 conditions are met.

**Pushback:** Make Completion conditional upon:

- effective written change-control consent from Bluefen;
- consent in a form and substance reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer;
- evidence that every condition to that consent has been satisfied or validly waived;
- no material adverse amendment, fee, concession or waiver being imposed without Buyer approval; and
- the consent remaining effective at Completion.

Delivery alone must not deem the condition satisfied. The Buyer should be able to waive the condition expressly, but should not be forced to complete on reasonable endeavours alone.

---

### 10. Riverlark facility and security

**Facts disclosed:** Approximately AUD 3.2 million remains outstanding; it has not been repaid and no final security discharge has been provided.

**Seller position:** Release following Completion.

**Departure:** The playbook requires current payout information, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. There is no approval for a post-Completion release.

**Pushback:** Require:

- an up-to-date Riverlark payout letter, including principal, interest, break costs and fees;
- irrevocable payment directions;
- direct payment to Riverlark from Completion funds;
- effective releases and discharges of all Company and asset security at Completion;
- termination or release of guarantees, control arrangements and financing authorities; and
- all required registry discharge documents and filing authority.

If any release is necessarily delivered after Completion, it requires both an irrevocable lender undertaking in an agreed form and Amelia Frost’s approval. Neither is presently available. “Approximately AUD 3.2 million” is insufficient for Completion funds flow.

---

### 11. Employee Completion bonuses

**Facts disclosed:** AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses is omitted from the draft funds flow, and the position on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs is unknown.

**Seller position:** These are a Seller matter and need not be separately itemised.

**Concern:** If the Company pays the amounts after Completion, the economic burden may fall on the Buyer despite the bonuses being triggered by the transaction. The omission also prevents verification that the debt-free/cash-free price mechanics deal with the liability correctly.

**Pushback:** Require either:

- payment and discharge by the Seller outside the Company; or
- a specific funds-flow line item, funded from Seller proceeds, for AUD 420,000 plus all applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other triggered on-costs.

Obtain a calculation of on-costs and confirmation of recipients, conditions and payment timing. Include an indemnity for any related liability not fully funded at Completion. Avoid double counting under any debt or working-capital mechanism.

---

### 12. Ironquay IP

**Facts disclosed:** Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 as open, but this is not independently verified; no receipt or confirmatory assignment is present.

**Seller position:** A narrow indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment is adequate.

**Departure:** The risk is not simply the amount of an unpaid invoice. It includes ownership, assignment, use rights, infringement exposure, remediation expense and operational disruption if the Company does not obtain the required IP.

**Pushback:**

- Preserve a specific SOW3 cure requiring verified payment and an effective assignment/confirmation of ownership or licence rights.
- Obtain an up-to-date statement directly from Ironquay or other independent payment evidence.
- Broaden the indemnity to cover losses arising from failure to obtain the relevant SOW3 rights, unpaid fees, ownership or assignment defects, third-party claims and necessary remediation.
- Keep the indemnity outside the general Warranty Claim basket and cap unless a separate, expressly negotiated IP regime is agreed.

Do not accept AUD 180,000 as conclusively owed or conclusively sufficient; it remains unverified.

---

### 13. Export/privacy incident

**Facts disclosed:** A download link was sent to an unintended external address and may concern about 1,240 records. Access, exact scope, notification obligations and loss have not been established.

**Seller position:** Preliminary and not expected to be material.

**Assessment:** The Seller’s materiality conclusion is unsupported, but the current record also does not justify characterising this as a confirmed breach, assuming a notification obligation or asserting a numerical loss.

**Pushback:** Require:

- preservation of all relevant logs, emails, access records and forensic evidence;
- a documented investigation by appropriately qualified personnel;
- prompt updates and production of investigation results;
- consultation with the Buyer before regulator or affected-person notifications, subject to law;
- no deletion, alteration, admission or settlement without appropriate Buyer involvement;
- confirmation of containment measures and any access or download evidence; and
- a Completion update and tailored protection for pre-Completion conduct and remediation costs, depending on the investigation outcome.

The SPA drafting should remain fact-neutral and should not state either that a breach occurred or that the issue is immaterial.

---

### 14. Sandbar supplier renewals

**Facts disclosed:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each, aggregating AUD 330,000. It is unclear whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Seller position:** Ordinary-course operating costs.

**Assessment:** Neither automatic Debt treatment nor automatic acceptance is justified on the current evidence.

**Pushback:** Obtain the contracts, renewal dates, termination rights, service periods, accrual treatment, payment status and business need. Determine whether the commitments are:

- ordinary-course costs reflected in working capital;
- prepaid expenses;
- accrued liabilities;
- non-cancellable commitments; or
- exceptional commitments entered into before Completion.

Any purchase-price treatment should follow that assessment and avoid double counting. Do not accept the Seller’s label as determinative, but do not impose an automatic AUD 330,000 deduction without analysis.

---

### 15. Evidence of title

**Seller position:** DD-012, the Company’s internal share register, proves ownership of 100% of the shares.

**Departure:** The playbook requires independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. An internal register is a relevant source but is not independent proof.

**Pushback:** Require a title package including:

- original or replacement share certificates;
- ASIC searches and current and historical company extracts;
- PPSR and other relevant Encumbrance searches against the Seller and Company;
- constitutional documents and relevant shareholder resolutions;
- evidence of the chain of allotments and transfers;
- confirmation of no options, convertibles, trusts, nominees or third-party rights;
- Seller corporate authority and signing approvals; and
- executed transfers and delivery of unencumbered title at Completion.

Maintain full title warranties notwithstanding the Buyer’s verification exercise.

---

### 16. Office lease and Mossvale

The specific disclosures suggest:

- the office lease may require notification, but is not presently shown to require consent; and
- Mossvale restricts assignment, but the disclosed provision does not appear to require consent merely for a share sale.

We should not overstate either issue. Instead:

- review the full agreements for change-of-control, deemed assignment, termination and notification provisions;
- ensure any required notification is made on time; and
- require confirmation that no undisclosed side letter or related provision changes the analysis.

These matters do not presently justify treating either consent as a Completion condition without further contractual support.

---

### 17. Stale and incomplete diligence record

The general disclosures are dated as at 5.00 pm on 22 September 2026. Several matters are expressly preliminary or unverified.

**Pushback:** Require a refreshed factual record, including:

- final Bluefen consent and satisfaction evidence;
- current Riverlark payout and release documents;
- current Ironquay balance and IP cure evidence;
- bonus on-cost calculations;
- an updated incident investigation;
- Sandbar contract/payment analysis; and
- updated title and Encumbrance searches.

No update should automatically qualify the warranties merely because it is delivered before Completion. The SPA must specify the effect of supplemental disclosure and preserve Buyer remedies for material new matters.

## Recommended negotiating position

### Non-negotiable or highest-priority points

1. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-outs from every limitation and remedy restriction.
2. Separate title/fundamental regime: 100% cap, at least six years, no basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
3. Effective Bluefen consent, including satisfaction of its conditions, before Completion.
4. Riverlark repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases at Completion.
5. Specific fair disclosure only; no whole-data-room or public-register deemed disclosure.
6. Remove constructive Buyer knowledge and broad adviser-knowledge exclusions.
7. Preserve distinct regimes for Tax, IP, indemnities, payment obligations and covenants.

### Opening economic/liability position

- General warranty cap: AUD 6 million / 25%.
- General claims period: 24 months.
- De minimis: AUD 5,000.
- Basket: AUD 50,000, tipping to first-dollar recovery.

Neither the 20% cap nor the 18-month period is currently authorised.

### Matter-specific protections

- Seller-fund the AUD 420,000 bonuses plus all on-costs.
- Verify and cure the Ironquay SOW3 position and broaden the indemnity.
- Preserve evidence and complete the DD-006 investigation without assuming a breach or loss.
- Investigate the Sandbar renewals before deciding their price-mechanics treatment.
- Obtain independent title and Encumbrance evidence rather than relying solely on DD-012.

Overall, the Seller’s draft transfers too much known and unknown risk to the Buyer while substantially narrowing the Buyer’s remedies. It should be marked up on a category-by-category basis rather than negotiated as the “fair and balanced package” asserted by the Seller.

Tax and IP remain open; they have not been settled merely because the Seller says so.

**Pushback:** Replace the blanket language with a clear liability matrix. Each cap, threshold and time limit should identify the claim category to which it applies. Preserve distinct regimes for:

1. general Warranty Claims;
2. title/fundamental claims;
3. Tax Claims;
4. IP claims and specific IP indemnities;
5. specific indemnities;
6. payment and price-adjustment obligations; and
7. covenant claims.

No unlimited Tax or IP liability should be conceded merely by rejecting the Seller’s general regime; those terms remain to be negotiated.

---

### 7. Disclosure standard

**Seller position:** Everything contained or referred to in the data room, statutory registers and public records is generally disclosed.

**Departure:** The playbook requires specific fair disclosure and rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.

A blanket disclosure makes the Buyer responsible for identifying the legal significance of documents spread across the data room. Public availability likewise does not establish that a matter was fairly disclosed against a particular warranty.

**Pushback:**

- Delete paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2 as general warranty disclosures.
- Require each exception to identify the relevant warranty and fairly disclose the nature and scope of the matter, including enough detail to understand its likely consequences.
- Data-room documents may support a specific disclosure only if clearly identified and cross-referenced.
- Reject disclosure by material merely “referred to” elsewhere.
- Reject public-register deemed disclosure and any prudent-search concept.
- Require a final indexed data-room copy and prohibit later alteration.
- Any supplemental disclosure should require Buyer review and should not automatically qualify warranties or remove termination rights.

The Seller’s reservation that disclosure does not admit breach or liability can remain only if it does not diminish the contractual fair-disclosure standard or the operative protections agreed for the relevant matter.

---

### 8. Buyer knowledge

**Seller position:** No claim for anything known by the Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records.

**Departure:** This is an impermissible constructive-knowledge and adviser-knowledge exclusion. It also duplicates the Seller’s overbroad disclosure regime.

**Pushback:** Delete the blanket knowledge exclusion. If any knowledge qualifier is retained:

- it should apply only to the actual knowledge of specifically named individuals;
- constructive knowledge, adviser knowledge and “discoverable” matters should be excluded;
- the Seller’s own warranty knowledge qualifiers should use named Seller knowledge persons who have made reasonable enquiries; and
- no knowledge bar should apply to title, capacity, authority, fraud, deliberate concealment or specific indemnities.

Buyer diligence should not relieve the Seller of responsibility for contractual warranties.

---

### 9. Bluefen consent

**Facts disclosed:** Bluefen represents approximately AUD 3.6 million of FY26 revenue, roughly 30%. The final written consent and evidence of satisfaction of its conditions are absent.

**Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent.

**Departure:** Given Bluefen’s materiality, reasonable endeavours and mere delivery are inadequate. A document called a consent may be conditional, revocable or ineffective unless clause 11.3 conditions are met.

**Pushback:** Make Completion conditional upon:

- effective written change-control consent from Bluefen;
- consent in a form and substance reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer;
- evidence that every condition to that consent has been satisfied or validly waived;
- no material adverse amendment, fee, concession or waiver being imposed without Buyer approval; and
- the consent remaining effective at Completion.

Delivery alone must not deem the condition satisfied. The Buyer should be able to waive the condition expressly, but should not be forced to complete on reasonable endeavours alone.

### 10. Riverlark facility and security

**Facts disclosed:** Approximately AUD 3.2 million remains outstanding; it has not been repaid and no final security discharge has been provided.

**Seller position:** Release following Completion.

**Departure:** The playbook requires current payout information, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. There is no approval for a post-Completion release.

**Pushback:** Require:

- an up-to-date Riverlark payout letter, including principal, interest, break costs and fees;
- irrevocable payment directions;
- direct payment to Riverlark from Completion funds;
- effective releases and discharges of all Company and asset security at Completion;
- termination or release of guarantees, control arrangements and financing authorities; and
- all required registry discharge documents and filing authority.

If any release is necessarily delivered after Completion, it requires both an irrevocable lender undertaking in an agreed form and Amelia Frost’s approval. Neither is presently available. “Approximately AUD 3.2 million” is insufficient for Completion funds flow.

### 11. Employee Completion bonuses

**Facts disclosed:** AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses is omitted from the draft funds flow, and the position on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs is unknown.

**Seller position:** These are a Seller matter and need not be separately itemised.

**Concern:** If the Company pays the amounts after Completion, the economic burden may fall on the Buyer despite the bonuses being triggered by the transaction. The omission also prevents verification that the debt-free/cash-free price mechanics deal with the liability correctly.

**Pushback:** Require either:

- payment and discharge by the Seller outside the Company; or
- a specific funds-flow line item, funded from Seller proceeds, for AUD 420,000 plus all applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other triggered on-costs.

Obtain a calculation of on-costs and confirmation of recipients, conditions and payment timing. Include an indemnity for any related liability not fully funded at Completion. Avoid double counting under any debt or working-capital mechanism.

### 12. Ironquay IP

**Facts disclosed:** Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 as open, but this is not independently verified; no receipt or confirmatory assignment is present.

**Seller position:** A narrow indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment is adequate.

**Departure:** The risk is not simply the amount of an unpaid invoice. It includes ownership, assignment, use rights, infringement exposure, remediation expense and operational disruption if the Company does not obtain the required IP.

**Pushback:**

- Preserve a specific SOW3 cure requiring verified payment and an effective assignment/confirmation of ownership or licence rights.
- Obtain an up-to-date statement directly from Ironquay or other independent payment evidence.
- Broaden the indemnity to cover losses arising from failure to obtain the relevant SOW3 rights, unpaid fees, ownership or assignment defects, third-party claims and necessary remediation.
- Keep the indemnity outside the general Warranty Claim basket and cap unless a separate, expressly negotiated IP regime is agreed.

Do not accept AUD 180,000 as conclusively owed or conclusively sufficient; it remains unverified.

### 13. Export/privacy incident

**Facts disclosed:** A download link was sent to an unintended external address and may concern about 1,240 records. Access, exact scope, notification obligations and loss have not been established.

**Seller position:** Preliminary and not expected to be material.

**Assessment:** The Seller’s materiality conclusion is unsupported, but the current record also does not justify characterising this as a confirmed breach, assuming a notification obligation or asserting a numerical loss.

**Pushback:** Require:

- preservation of all relevant logs, emails, access records and forensic evidence;
- a documented investigation by appropriately qualified personnel;
- prompt updates and production of investigation results;
- consultation with the Buyer before regulator or affected-person notifications, subject to law;
- no deletion, alteration, admission or settlement without appropriate Buyer involvement;
- confirmation of containment measures and any access or download evidence; and
- a Completion update and tailored protection for pre-Completion conduct and remediation costs, depending on the investigation outcome.

The SPA drafting should remain fact-neutral and should not state either that a breach occurred or that the issue is immaterial.

### 14. Sandbar supplier renewals

**Facts disclosed:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each, aggregating AUD 330,000. It is unclear whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Seller position:** Ordinary-course operating costs.

**Assessment:** Neither automatic Debt treatment nor automatic acceptance is justified on the current evidence.

**Pushback:** Obtain the contracts, renewal dates, termination rights, service periods, accrual treatment, payment status and business need. Determine whether the commitments are:

- ordinary-course costs reflected in working capital;
- prepaid expenses;
- accrued liabilities;
- non-cancellable commitments; or
- exceptional commitments entered into before Completion.

Any purchase-price treatment should follow that assessment and avoid double counting. Do not accept the Seller’s label as determinative, but do not impose an automatic AUD 330,000 deduction without analysis.

### 15. Evidence of title

**Seller position:** DD-012, the Company’s internal share register, proves ownership of 100% of the shares.

**Departure:** The playbook requires independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. An internal register is a relevant source but is not independent proof.

**Pushback:** Require a title package including:

- original or replacement share certificates;
- ASIC searches and current and historical company extracts;
- PPSR and other relevant Encumbrance searches against the Seller and Company;
- constitutional documents and relevant shareholder resolutions;
- evidence of the chain of allotments and transfers;
- confirmation of no options, convertibles, trusts, nominees or third-party rights;
- Seller corporate authority and signing approvals; and
- executed transfers and delivery of unencumbered title at Completion.

Maintain full title warranties notwithstanding the Buyer’s verification exercise.

The specific disclosures suggest:

The general disclosures are dated as at 5.00 pm on 22 September 2026. Several matters are expressly preliminary or unverified.

**Pushback:** Require a refreshed factual record, including:

- final Bluefen consent and satisfaction evidence;
- current Riverlark payout and release documents;
- current Ironquay balance and IP cure evidence;

No update should automatically qualify the warranties merely because it is delivered before Completion. The SPA must specify the effect of supplemental disclosure and preserve Buyer remedies for material new matters.

## Recommended negotiating position

### Non-negotiable or highest-priority points

1. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-outs from every limitation and remedy restriction.
2. Separate title/fundamental regime: 100% cap, at least six years, no basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
3. Effective Bluefen consent, including satisfaction of its conditions, before Completion.
4. Riverlark repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases at Completion.
5. Specific fair disclosure only; no whole-data-room or public-register deemed disclosure.
6. Remove constructive Buyer knowledge and broad adviser-knowledge exclusions.
7. Preserve distinct regimes for Tax, IP, indemnities, payment obligations and covenants.

### Opening economic/liability position

- General warranty cap: AUD 6 million / 25%.
- General claims period: 24 months.
- De minimis: AUD 5,000.
- Basket: AUD 50,000, tipping to first-dollar recovery.

Neither the 20% cap nor the 18-month period is currently authorised.

### Matter-specific protections

- Seller-fund the AUD 420,000 bonuses plus all on-costs.
- Verify and cure the Ironquay SOW3 position and broaden the indemnity.
- Preserve evidence and complete the DD-006 investigation without assuming a breach or loss.
- Investigate the Sandbar renewals before deciding their price-mechanics treatment.
- Obtain independent title and Encumbrance evidence rather than relying solely on DD-012.

Overall, the Seller’s draft transfers too much known and unknown risk to the Buyer while substantially narrowing the Buyer’s remedies. It should be marked up on a category-by-category basis rather than negotiated as the “fair and balanced package” asserted by the Seller.
